title: agentarch control
description: One verifiable rule. Every control has a prose counterpart in content/standards/; validate checks that correspondence in both directions, so a control cannot exist without an explanation and a documented rule cannot exist without a check.

intent.description: Why this exists, in terms of what goes wrong without it. A control whose intent cannot be stated in one sentence is usually two controls.

status.description: Lifecycle stage. No control is born blocking; see spec/normative/08-versioning.md.

applies_to.description: Narrows where the control is evaluated at all. Absent means everywhere.

kind.description: Closed set. A pack is data, never code — there is no kind that runs something.

expr.description: Restricted expression, per spec/normative/04-expression-language.md. Required for static_manifest and eval_threshold.

path_expr.description: For file_exists: an expression yielding the path to test, relative to the agent directory.

message.description: Shown when the control fails. State what is wrong, not that something is wrong.

evidence.description: What proves the control. manifest_field alone means the control verifies a declaration, which is legitimate — `owner_defined` is exactly that and should block. The constraint is on the pack, not the control: a pack whose blockers are all manifest_field is a form to fill in, so at least one must rest on an executable artifact. `score` reports declared and proven separately for this reason.

remediation.description: What to do about it. A finding without a remediation trains people to ignore findings.

standard_ref.description: Path and anchor of the prose counterpart. Verified by AA-DOC-008.

references.description: External framework mappings, e.g. "OWASP LLM06". Mappings only — never the source text.
